pass_a_gloss:
It is written that if we walk in the light, we have communion with God and the Father, and the blood of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, cleanses us from all sin. We have been cleansed by the holy blood of our Savior Christ, who sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high, after making purification through his blood, and has become superior to the angels, inheriting a more excellent name, for he is called the Son. The Word became flesh, yet remained the radiance of the Father's glory and the exact representation of his being, not making his own nature separate from the economy with flesh, in order to bear our sufferings. He endured the cross, despising shame, and insults, and blows, in order to free us from all defilement, making us clean by his own blood, and to join us to God and the Father through himself, for through him we have access, and he is the door and the way. Although the Word became flesh and dwelled among us, making his own body from the holy virgin, yet he was in glory and in the nature of divinity, and did not depart from the thrones of the Father. He was a man on earth, yet filled heaven again, and all things were full of him. He was made a little lower than the angels, because of the measure of humanity, for human nature is inferior to that of the angels.

He was and is above all authority and power and dominion and every name that is named not only in this age but also in the one to come. And knowing this, the divine Paul writes that we know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who being rich became poor for us, so that we might become rich through his poverty. He became so much better than the angels. For 'Angel' is a name of ministry and indicates a domestic measure to us. But 'Son' shows the substantial and natural existence from the Father. Therefore, he did not say 'greater' or 'more honorable' comparatively, so that someone might not think of these and those as of the same kind. But he said 'better', so that the difference of the Son's nature to the created things might be known. And we have proof of these things from the divine scriptures, with David singing that one day in God's courts is better than a thousand, and Solomon proclaiming that wisdom is better than precious stones. How are wisdom and earthly stones not of a different substance and nature? What kinship is there between the heavenly courts and earthly houses? Thus, there is no kinship between the Son and the angels. Since there is no kinship, the 'better' was not spoken comparatively, but distinctively because of the difference of his nature from theirs.
pass_b_english: Through the blood of Jesus Christ, we have been cleansed from all sin, and we have communion with God and the Father (1 John 1:7). This is because the Word became flesh, yet remained the radiance of the Father's glory and the exact representation of his being, and he endured the cross, despising shame, and insults, and blows, in order to free us from all defilement. As the Son of God, he has become superior to the angels, inheriting a more excellent name, and he is the door and the way to God and the Father (John 14:6). Although he was made a little lower than the angels, because of the measure of humanity, he was in glory and in the nature of divinity, and did not depart from the thrones of the Father. He was a man on earth, yet filled heaven again, and all things were full of him, and through him we have access to God and the Father.

The Word, who is the radiance of the Father's glory and the exact representation of his being, became flesh and dwelled among us, making his own body from the holy virgin (John 1:14). He endured the sufferings of humanity, including the cross, shame, and insults, in order to cleanse us from all sin and join us to God and the Father through himself. As our Savior, he has sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high, and he is the one through whom we have access to God and the Father, and he is the door and the way.

Christ's supremacy is evident in his position above all authority, power, and dominion, as well as every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the one to come (Ephesians 1:21). The apostle Paul, aware of this, writes about the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who, despite being rich, became poor for our sake, so that we might become rich through his poverty (2 Corinthians 8:9). This makes him far superior to the angels.

The terms 'Angel' and 'Son' have distinct meanings, with 'Angel' signifying a name of ministry and indicating a domestic measure, while 'Son' reveals the substantial and natural existence from the Father. Therefore, he did not say 'greater' or 'more honorable' comparatively, so that someone might not think of these and those as of the same kind. But he said 'better', so that the difference in the Son's nature to the created things might be known. This is supported by scripture, where David sings that one day in God's courts is better than a thousand (Psalm 84:10), and Solomon proclaims that wisdom is better than precious stones (Proverbs 3:15). How are wisdom and earthly stones not of a different substance and nature? What kinship is there between the heavenly courts and earthly houses? Thus, there is no kinship between the Son and the angels. Since there is no kinship, the 'better' was not spoken comparatively, but distinctively because of the difference of his nature from theirs.
